programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In this episode, conservation is the focus. The team are pinning their hopes on a precious white-backed vulture chick, a species facing extinction in the wild. If they can successfully raise this chick, its survival could help secure the future of these vital scavengers. But with first-time parents and memories of past issues, can the keepers risk returning it to the nest? Elsewhere, the park’s pack of rare African painted dogs are put to the ultimate test in a feeding challenge designed to encourage their natural teamwork, with spectacular results. Hamza helps carry out a health check on an elusive capybara who refuses to play ball, and there’s joy as a tamarin family show their wild side with a sticky tree sap treat. Meanwhile, the wolf pack face their own battle. Can the keepers help them lose their winter coats before the summer heat puts them in danger?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: There’s a chase through the streets of Croydon, south London, when a car’s stolen by suspected drug dealers. A team of specialist vehicle trackers, led by former police officer Neil, are called in to hunt down the vehicle and help recover it. As a dramatic pursuit unfolds, Neil meets the stolen car head-on. Meanwhile, tracker Richard sets up an elaborate sting operation to catch criminals responsible for stealing plant machinery worth tens of thousands of pounds. But will they fall into the trap? In Dudley, Nadine has her BMW convertible stolen off her driveway late at night. She only discovers it’s gone when her husband goes out to walk the dog the following morning. It looks like the thieves are long-gone. But Nadine and her husband aren’t giving up that easily. They tap into the car’s tracking app and quickly pick up a GPS signal which gives them the car’s location. All they need to do now is get it back.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A mother and her son vanish in 1976, leaving just a burnt-out car. Forty years later, a blood analyst helps police find out the truth. And a phone analyst helps find the killer of a drowned man.

programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Presenter Natasha Raskin Sharp is at Sandown Racecourse in Surrey. Natasha looks at a collection of accessories dating from the late 1700s to the 1960s belonging to and donated by local people.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. Three old chairs bring tears to the eyes, furniture upcycler Sarah dreams up a wild new look for a side table, and Jacqui's imagination is on fire as she wrestles a plant stand - but will all three items produce profits for their unsuspecting owners?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having grown out of their town flat, two newlyweds with a budget of £400,000 need Ginny Buckley’s help to find a new home in the Dorset countryside that has enough space to keep bicycles, golf clubs and surfboards out of sight. On the world-famous Jurassic Coast, Ginny also meets a lifelong fossil hunter, whose impressive treasures are now housed in a purpose-built museum near the coast where they were discovered.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: In this episode, conservation is the focus. The team are pinning their hopes on a precious white-backed vulture chick, a species facing extinction in the wild. If they can successfully raise this chick, its survival could help secure the future of these vital scavengers. But with first-time parents and memories of past issues, can the keepers risk returning it to the nest? Elsewhere, the park’s pack of rare African painted dogs are put to the ultimate test in a feeding challenge designed to encourage their natural teamwork, with spectacular results. Hamza helps carry out a health check on an elusive capybara who refuses to play ball, and there’s joy as a tamarin family show their wild side with a sticky tree sap treat. Meanwhile, the wolf pack face their own battle. Can the keepers help them lose their winter coats before the summer heat puts them in danger?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: There’s a chase through the streets of Croydon, south London, when a car’s stolen by suspected drug dealers. A team of specialist vehicle trackers, led by former police officer Neil, are called in to hunt down the vehicle and help recover it. As a dramatic pursuit unfolds, Neil meets the stolen car head-on. Meanwhile, tracker Richard sets up an elaborate sting operation to catch criminals responsible for stealing plant machinery worth tens of thousands of pounds. But will they fall into the trap? In Dudley, Nadine has her BMW convertible stolen off her driveway late at night. She only discovers it’s gone when her husband goes out to walk the dog the following morning. It looks like the thieves are long-gone. But Nadine and her husband aren’t giving up that easily. They tap into the car’s tracking app and quickly pick up a GPS signal which gives them the car’s location. All they need to do now is get it back.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A mother and her son vanish in 1976, leaving just a burnt-out car. Forty years later, a blood analyst helps police find out the truth. And a phone analyst helps find the killer of a drowned man.

Natasha looks at a collection of accessories dating from the late 1700s to the 1960s belonging to and donated by local people.

programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. On the world-famous Jurassic Coast, Ginny also meets a lifelong fossil hunter, whose impressive treasures are now housed in a purpose-built museum near the coast where they were discovered.

programme.title: The Bidding Room

Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

Elsewhere, the park’s pack of rare African painted dogs are put to the ultimate test in a feeding challenge designed to encourage their natural teamwork, with spectacular results. Hamza helps carry out a health check on an elusive capybara who refuses to play ball, and there’s joy as a tamarin family show their wild side with a sticky tree sap treat. Meanwhile, the wolf pack face their own battle. Can the keepers help them lose their winter coats before the summer heat puts them in danger?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: There’s a chase through the streets of Croydon, south London, when a car’s stolen by suspected drug dealers. A team of specialist vehicle trackers, led by former police officer Neil, are called in to hunt down the vehicle and help recover it. As a dramatic pursuit unfolds, Neil meets the stolen car head-on. Meanwhile, tracker Richard sets up an elaborate sting operation to catch criminals responsible for stealing plant machinery worth tens of thousands of pounds. But will they fall into the trap? In Dudley, Nadine has her BMW convertible stolen off her driveway late at night. She only discovers it’s gone when her husband goes out to walk the dog the following morning. It looks like the thieves are long-gone. But Nadine and her husband aren’t giving up that easily. They tap into the car’s tracking app and quickly pick up a GPS signal which gives them the car’s location. All they need to do now is get it back.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A mother and her son vanish in 1976, leaving just a burnt-out car. Forty years later, a blood analyst helps police find out the truth. And a phone analyst helps find the killer of a drowned man.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Presenter Natasha Raskin Sharp is at Sandown Racecourse in Surrey. With the expert help of Charles Hanson and Thomas Forrester, the reds and the blues battle it out to see who can buy the most profitable three items to take to auction. Natasha looks at a collection of accessories dating from the late 1700s to the 1960s belonging to and donated by local people.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. Three old chairs bring tears to the eyes, furniture upcycler Sarah dreams up a wild new look for a side table, and Jacqui's imagination is on fire as she wrestles a plant stand - but will all three items produce profits for their unsuspecting owners?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having grown out of their town flat, two newlyweds with a budget of £400,000 need Ginny Buckley’s help to find a new home in the Dorset countryside that has enough space to keep bicycles, golf clubs and surfboards out of sight. On the world-famous Jurassic Coast, Ginny also meets a lifelong fossil hunter, whose impressive treasures are now housed in a purpose-built museum near the coast where they were discovered.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Unusual items from Africa and a Victorian tea caddy head to auction. JB and Lauren’s trip to Sussex brings surprising finds that could help send a family on holiday.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
programme.desc: On a daily basis, Roman Kemp is contacted by young people who are struggling. With people turning to him for advice, he’s questioning whether or not there is a worsening mental health crisis and asking if these young people should be offered more support in their own communities. This documentary follows Roman as he immerses himself in schools, youth centres and treatment settings around the country, meets with experts and charities, and visits the Houses of Parliament to try to understand the potential solutions for improving the mental health of young people in the UK today.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall takes to the icy waters of British Columbia in search of the biggest, baddest sea lion in the world. After an unexpected encounter with a killer whale, he heads back to the city on the trail of one smelly contender before trying his hand at becoming a raccoon. Despite immense strength, powerful claws and a fearsome reputation in Canada, there's a surprise in store when Steve tracks down the infamous black bear.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In this episode of the world's biggest car programme, Richard Hammond is dropped into the remote, frozen wastes of Canada to test a watch with a built-in emergency beacon. Normally, activating the device would summon a vast international rescue crew, but in Hammond's case, the distress signal is sent directly to Jeremy Clarkson and James May who are disorganised, disinterested and very many miles away. Eventually, the pair get their hands on two machines they believe are suitable for the job and set off on an epic adventure to find their colleague. Also in this show, Clarkson is on the track in the new 471-horsepower Lexus RC F coupe whilst star of The Fall and The X-Files Gillian Anderson tries her hand in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: In the mood to torment the Traitors, Karine sets out to test their skills by issuing the famous Murder in Plain Sight challenge. With a cursed shield hidden in the manor, one poor Faithful might find devastation in lieu of protection, but only if a Traitor can get it into their hands. With the pressure of Karine’s expectations looming, one false step could prove fatal for the Traitors.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: In a game that relies on words, the guests learn they are not always guaranteed the right to speak. For one player, the privilege is completely revoked when they find themselves unable to defend their game at the Round Table. While the other players don’t face the same limitations, they quickly learn that their choice of words can cut in ways they never intended.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: After loudly proclaiming to be the most loyal of the loyal, it can be difficult to betray one's own beliefs - but for one guest, they may have no other choice. Having come so far in the game, appearing unaffected may be the hardest challenge yet.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: With the aftershocks of lies and betrayal lingering in the manor, the heat is on for the remaining guests to make their final moves before the Fire of Truth determines who will claim the prize pot – the Traitors or the Faithful.

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: As the Department of Justice closes in, Amanda insists she is still ill. But when charges are filed, the truth is tested in court.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. She enlists carpenter Ollie to overhaul a coffee table, but will his bonkers plan including concrete and a traffic cone prove to be a winner? For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers and Simon Bower are stunned as one of Scotland’s most famous figures comes to light, a polished yet practical piece is up for sale, and the dealers are moved by a family story of wartime courage.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the first ever RHS Sandringham Flower Show, and Arit Anderson, Jamie Butterworth and Frances Tophill are on hand to take a look around. From spectacular show gardens to a floral marquee packed full of horticultural goodies, there is something to whet the appetite. A local grower who knows everything there is to know about roses provides expert advice, while a National Collection holder in Lincolnshire shines a light on drought-tolerant achilleas. A couple in Kent share their new-found love of succulents, with some useful advice on how to care for them. And in Hampshire, a plantsman conveys his passion for carrying on the family tradition of running a nursery.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The halfway point of the Hairy Bikers' Bakeation sees them journey to the furthest reaches of Europe culminating in an amazing family party thrown by Dave's wife Lil, who comes from Romania. Three countries, Slovakia, Hungary and Romania, provide the Bikers with ample opportunity to explore some great baking. It all starts in a café in Bratislava, where the Bikers are served three cakes which, believe it or not, are inspired by British TV cookery shows. They also have an encounter with kremesh, the Hungarian take on a vanilla slice, served in a café that survived the ravages of communism; langos, a roadside snack of deep-fried pastry with sour cream and cheese, and Tokaj wine, the choice of kings once more prized than any wine made in France. The Bikers keep their end of the culinary deal with zemlovka, an Eastern European take on the classic bread and butter pudding, some amazing cheese and bacon savoury scones, a robust goulash stew and a curly pie made especially for the family party in Romania.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Sheep farmer James is proud that his 12-year-old son Charlie seems to be following in his farming footsteps. They are also both passionate about running their beloved sheepdogs and are heading to the prestigious Macclesfield sheepdog trials. It’s a magnet for the country’s best sheepdog triallists, who try their luck at winning a place on the national team. Also hoping to add to his huge trophy collection is Cumbrian farmer and auctioneer Ross, with his teenage son Oliver. While both sons manage to keep their cool and control their dogs, their experienced fathers must overcome pre-trial nerves, a challenging course, difficult sheep and bad weather.

programme.title: Earth from Space
programme.desc: Cameras in space tell stories of life on our planet from a brand new perspective. At a time when the Earth’s surface is changing faster than ever in human history, watch cities grow, forest disappear and glaciers melt. In the ever-growing grey of cities one man is feeding thousands of parakeets; in Sumatra a female orang-utan and her daughter face life in a forest under threat; while in Tanzania local people use satellites to replant a forest, securing the future for a family of chimpanzees. This is our home as we’ve never seen it before.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Oxford Union, a mecca for debate right in the heart of the city. Paul Martin is joined by experts Will Axon and Mark Stacey. Together they pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at the local auction house. Will meets his match when he comes across a World War I bayonet, while Mark is given a run for his money when it comes to knowledge about Royal Doulton. Paul gets down with the birth of rock 'n' roll through the work of music photographer Harry Hammond.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Can a sweet treat ever be good for you? Zoe Ball is in Birmingham, trying to tempt fitness fanatic Bilal away from sugary sweets and towards flavanol-rich dark chocolate. Chocolate may get a bad press, but the science shows that if you go over to the dark side and eat chocolate with at least 70 per cent cocoa, it could boost your heart health, improve your brain function and even reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes. A delicious upgrade with serious benefits.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Ginny Buckley presents an arresting range of houses to a couple who have a substantial budget of £700,000 and are hoping to relocate their family to the wonderful Norfolk countryside. For over half a century, Norfolk has also been home to Lotus cars, so whilst in the county Ginny finds out more about the company heritage before catching a glimpse of the future when their latest hypercar is unveiled.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: In central England, an RAF airbase with a Roman past, a forgotten medieval nunnery, a gold pendant from a 7th-century grave and a pub with a very long history of hospitality.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: Winter on the moors is tough, although the sheep for whom they are home have been bred to cope with the cold and snow better than most, even the ewes who are pregnant at this time of year.

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Adam Fleming.

programme.title: Golf: Women's Open
programme.desc: Highlights of the opening day of the Women’s Open from Royal Lytham & St Annes. South Korea’s Haeran Ryu is going for a third consecutive major victory, with American world number one Nelly Korda also looking to make it a hat-trick of major wins this season. England’s Georgia Hall returns to the scene of her famous win in 2018, with world number five Lottie Woad and world number seven Charlie Hull also on home soil looking to land their first major titles. Japan’s Miyu Yamashita defends the trophy she won at Royal Porthcawl in 2025.

programme.title: The Blackening
programme.desc: Film horror comedy. A group of friends on a getaway discover that a killer, out for revenge, has planned the whole thing.

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: As the Department of Justice closes in, Amanda insists she is still ill. But when charges are filed, the truth is tested in court.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers and Simon Bower are stunned as one of Scotland’s most famous figures comes to light, a polished yet practical piece is up for sale, and the dealers are moved by a family story of wartime courage.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the first ever RHS Sandringham Flower Show, and Arit Anderson, Jamie Butterworth and Frances Tophill are on hand to take a look around. From spectacular show gardens to a floral marquee packed full of horticultural goodies, there is something to whet the appetite. A local grower who knows everything there is to know about roses provides expert advice, while a National Collection holder in Lincolnshire shines a light on drought-tolerant achilleas. A couple in Kent share their new-found love of succulents, with some useful advice on how to care for them. And in Hampshire, a plantsman conveys his passion for carrying on the family tradition of running a nursery.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The halfway point of the Hairy Bikers' Bakeation sees them journey to the furthest reaches of Europe culminating in an amazing family party thrown by Dave's wife Lil, who comes from Romania. Three countries, Slovakia, Hungary and Romania, provide the Bikers with ample opportunity to explore some great baking. It all starts in a café in Bratislava, where the Bikers are served three cakes which, believe it or not, are inspired by British TV cookery shows. They also have an encounter with kremesh, the Hungarian take on a vanilla slice, served in a café that survived the ravages of communism; langos, a roadside snack of deep-fried pastry with sour cream and cheese, and Tokaj wine, the choice of kings once more prized than any wine made in France. The Bikers keep their end of the culinary deal with zemlovka, an Eastern European take on the classic bread and butter pudding, some amazing cheese and bacon savoury scones, a robust goulash stew and a curly pie made especially for the family party in Romania.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Sheep farmer James is proud that his 12-year-old son Charlie seems to be following in his farming footsteps. They are also both passionate about running their beloved sheepdogs and are heading to the prestigious Macclesfield sheepdog trials. It’s a magnet for the country’s best sheepdog triallists, who try their luck at winning a place on the national team. Also hoping to add to his huge trophy collection is Cumbrian farmer and auctioneer Ross, with his teenage son Oliver. While both sons manage to keep their cool and control their dogs, their experienced fathers must overcome pre-trial nerves, a challenging course, difficult sheep and bad weather.

programme.title: Earth from Space
programme.desc: Cameras in space tell stories of life on our planet from a brand new perspective. At a time when the Earth’s surface is changing faster than ever in human history, watch cities grow, forest disappear and glaciers melt. In the ever-growing grey of cities one man is feeding thousands of parakeets; in Sumatra a female orang-utan and her daughter face life in a forest under threat; while in Tanzania local people use satellites to replant a forest, securing the future for a family of chimpanzees. This is our home as we’ve never seen it before.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Oxford Union, a mecca for debate right in the heart of the city. Paul Martin is joined by experts Will Axon and Mark Stacey. Will meets his match when he comes across a World War I bayonet, while Mark is given a run for his money when it comes to knowledge about Royal Doulton. programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Can a sweet treat ever be good for you? Zoe Ball is in Birmingham, trying to tempt fitness fanatic Bilal away from sugary sweets and towards flavanol-rich dark chocolate. Chocolate may get a bad press, but the science shows that if you go over to the dark side and eat chocolate with at least 70 per cent cocoa, it could boost your heart health, improve your brain function and even reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes. A delicious upgrade with serious benefits.

P, A, R, T and Y need some help getting the party started! S tries her best, but they really need someone extraordinary to liven things up and superhero Exciting X soon gets the party popping with his special powers.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piri gang enter a treasure hunt competition but discover they must pay Captain Krill with sprats for clues. Pancake is suspicious. Is there some fishy business going on?

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: After 799 years of winning the Great Gnome Games, Great Gnanna is worried she can't defend her title. To help, the doctors remind her that she is just as fearsome as ever.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: There’s a girder out of place on Swoppiton Bridge, and unless Nori can fix it, that bridge is coming down! Luckily, Mojo’s got the tops, and Bo’s got the skills to help get it done.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: 'Even when something breaks, you have to tell the truth so Flop knows what happened.' Bing is playing the talking lettuce game on Flop's phone when he drops the phone and accidentally breaks it. Too panicked to tell Flop what he has done, Bing puts the phone in the bin, but he's so upset that Flop knows something has happened.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘orange’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see an orange orange, some slices, a tasty one and meet a juicy orange! There’s an orange winning a football match and one spinning all around. The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Triggs is super excited to be visiting his favourite place in the world, the dog park, where he gets to hang out and play with all his doggy best friends. But when McGinty brings along a very nervous newcomer, Triggs sings a song to reassure her and encourage her to join in the fun.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: It’s Bear Berry Day! The Piggy Builders come up with a way to help Brian reach the top of the tree to pick berries on the special day. But Wilf wants the berries too...

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos visit a school hall. The teacher comes in and picks up a hoop and spins it. She picks up different coloured hoops and after spinning them she leaves them lying flat on the floor. The Twirlywoos set all the hoops spinning at the same time, the Hooter calls them back to the Big Red Boat. The teacher re-enters the school hall with five children and they are excited to see all the hoops spinning at once. The Robot visits the Twirlywoos. Chickedy and Chick turn the key on the robot's head, which makes the Robot spin. Great BigHoo turns the Robot's key and the Robot flies around the Big Red Boat, spinning as he goes. The Twirlywoos catch hold of the Robot and they too fly and spin around the Big Red Boat.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends go on a fruit picking adventure. Meanwhile, Aunt Polly judges the annual Fabulous Fruit Competition, but what has Mr Tumble done to Grandad’s strawberries?

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Laa-Laa and Po laugh themselves silly with a funny joke, but when they tell it to Dipsy, it doesn't tickle Dipsy in the same way. But Dipsy's funny dance does and when Dipsy dances again, the Teletubbies all laugh together. In Tummy Tales, children have fun being silly in a park.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies DJ, Holly, Li-Li, Luke, George, Otis and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Bowls which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate bowls inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun rhyme ‘Pat-a-cake’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children create binoculars using recycled tubes and decorations, learn British Sign Language signs for sailor, sea and see, then sing and sign A Sailor Went to Sea, Sea, Sea.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Nelly and Isla buzz around the garden and discover why bees collect nectar and pollen, before celebrating with a special bee dance to thank their buzzing friends.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Zawadi and Njamba the rhinos set out to explore the wild with their friend Bahati the zebra. Hamza finds a coypu and sets up a camera trap with Ranger Godfrey.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri gets upset and goes off in a huff.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Princesses, horses and magic wands. Bluey and Chloe can play any role they want, when they embark on an adventure to save their playground kingdom from the Greedy Queen.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are digging in the garden when they come across a fossil, so Duggee and Narrator explain all about fossils and prehistoric times. When the Squirrels go outside, it seems like they've gone right back in time.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Meet Lime! She’s in between Yellow and Green, fresh and full of zing! In this musical episode, Lime sings her heart out with her beloved electric guitar, loving the limelight.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Carys wants to find out all about jellyfish in today’s episode. Chantelle visits an aquarium which is home to some rather special jellyfish, whilst Rory meets a marine expert and they head out to sea on a glass-bottomed boat Chantelle and Rory’s fact files help answer all of Carys's questions. With the help of the Teeny Tiny Creatures poem we discover that, like lots of other teeny tiny creatures, jellyfish are superheroes and help our planet in their own special way. In the Teeny Tiny Task, Chantelle and the children pretend to be jellyfish with colourful ribbons.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: All rise for Queen Audrey! She plays a fun royal game and holds a special tea party for one of her favourite dolls. There are also lots of jewels and sparkles with some precious homemade necklaces. What will Mummy make of her glittery surprise? Later, the family heads out for a trip to the beach, where they have a splashing good time.

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Children’s cookery series with Big Cook Jen and Little Cook Small. Jen is birdwatching on a kitchen safari, while Small guesses which birds and animals they can see. Eric the Explorer visits the cafe for something to eat, so they cook him something exciting and unusual, just like the things Eric discovers in the wild.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he doesn’t hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel is Rayane’s ears. Together, they’re unstoppable! Diesel wakes up wondering where he is. Then, he remembers – he’s on a camping trip with Rayane and his friends Grace and Karim. And Mum’s come too! Rayane’s even made a dreamcatcher from sticks and leaves he found around the campsite. But now it’s time to go home, so there’s lots they need to do. After a breakfast of boiled eggs and toast, Diesel helps Rayane brush his teeth. It’s Diesel’s job to filter out all the other sounds at the campsite and let Rayane know when the timer goes off to let him know he’s brushed for long enough. Then, while the humans pack up camp, making sure not to leave any litter behind, Diesel has to listen out for Dad’s text so they can all meet him at the car park. The campers excitedly carry their kit back to meet Dad. But Rayane has left his dreamcatcher behind! Can Diesel follow the trail of familiar sounds to help Rayane find the campsite again – and collect Rayane’s missing dreamcatcher?

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: Mrs Farrell and Miss Gerrard are having a Kindness Day at school, a time when the class shows how they can be extra kind to each other. As the children start their day, they are thinking of new ideas to be super-kind. Jessica and Orla draw lovely pictures for the teachers, which makes Mrs Farrell and Miss Gerrard feel happy. At lunchtime, Solomon is finding the lid on his yogurt a bit tricky, so Sam helps him to open it! Outside, the children are tidying up the playground. Felicity sees that there is a queue for the climbing frame, so decides to let Bryn have a turn – how kind. Whilst climbing, Isla notices Bryn is struggling, so she helps him out with some top tips. At the end of the day, Mrs Farrell and Miss Gerrard give out certificates to those children who have been extra kind throughout the day.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is sad that Mrs Hobbs and her cat, George, are soon to leave Maple Close. The Brooklyn-Bells call on Mrs Hobbs to persuade her not to move house, only to find that her cat, George, has fleas. They offer to help and discover a secret about Mrs Hobbs.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Baba plan a surprise for Mama and Papa - they're going to collect some lovely, bright flowers for them! Baba comes across a honey bee in the meadow. Wherever bees are, there will be flowers, because they know where the best ones are! Oona, Baba and the bees find lots of beautiful flowers, but when they get to the Undergrowth, the pufflings see more bees than they bargained for.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes has borrowed Twinkle's xylophone, but he has lost it - and right before her performance! The gang race around the garden, listening for clues. But will they find it in time?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are off on a hill walk with Mum – but it’s just not the same without Dad. As they wander through the windy hills, they meet a new friend who introduces them to the wonders of yodelling. That gives Maddie an idea... maybe they can reach Dad after all?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Keith is excited to help the Piggies repair a fence, but it turns into a disaster. The little goat feels guilty. When they discover that Wilf is sabotaging everything, they can't let Keith give up!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The Numberblocks put on a talent show full of terrific number tricks, but it doesn't quite go according to plan. Learn all about the numbers 1 to 15 with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: O goes through the magnifying glass to where the grass is blue, the trees are square and nonsense words make friendly monsters who run off with magnifying glasses! This episode has fun with O and nonsense words, the word odd and the non-words og, yog, zog, zox and vox.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble looks for his pet dog's squeaky toy bone, while Justin spends the day with his friends and their pet dogs.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky puts Dipsy's hat in the bag - then Noo-noo hoovers them both up! The children in Tummy Tales pack a bag for an overnight stay with a relative, and the Teletubbies do a suitcase dance.

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Andy breaks a valuable museum artefact and has to travel back in time 30 million years to replace it. Landing in an age when giant mammals roamed the Earth, Andy tracks down the peculiar chalicothere and gets chased by a swarm of angry prehistoric hornets.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s stall. She chooses the toy whistle and remembers the day she got it… Moira has so many things to do. She wishes there were two of her to get everything done. When she sees Caitlin pretending to be her, it gives her an idea – Caitlin could become Mini Moira and help get things done around the Big Hub. Caitlin thinks this is a great idea, but Moira says being the manager at Big Hub isn’t as easy as it looks!

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies' very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that all help other machines! Grace drives a tugboat, shows off incredible refuelling planes and tows a bus in a recovery truck.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's pea crumble for lunch at Pup School, and when Biscuit gets peas stuck in her fur, Dodge mishears and thinks she has fleas. The misunderstanding sends the rest of the pups into a frenzy, thinking that fleas are spreading around the school. When Dodge takes a moment to double-check the facts, everything becomes clear.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea rexes help a Strawberrisaurus find courage for a special friendship dance.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: While collecting pictures, Dashi and Shellington get trapped in a flooding cave.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Cheeky Peter Rabbit loves adventure but he struggles to stay out of trouble. Luckily his best friends are always around to help him out. Based on Beatrix Potter's classic stories.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are off for a jamboree to make some new friends, play games and have a picnic. They meet another group of young animals with their very own version of Duggee, but everything they do is different - even Roly finds one of them too LOUD!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Daphne already wears glasses, but Vida thinks she might need another eye test.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: The veggies are playing walkie-talkie hide-and-seek, but Evil Pea steals Carrot’s walkie-talkie and uses it to trick the Veggies into getting trapped by the Corn Cobs.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy is excited about a new chip that will make his toy robot move on its own. When the Ducklings accidentally break the chip, they replace it with one from the Farm of the Future.

programme.title: Do Not Watch This Show
programme.desc: Wizz fears a scary monster is coming, but Nessie just wants to be his friend.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and her family are out of sorts, so Mum gets everyone to play musical statues.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey learns that adults take a little bit longer to make friends.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Twiggy has a funny tummy on the day of his performance. Nothing the doctors try works, not even the cure for froggy moths! Zog wonders if there is something else bothering Twiggy.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: When the ground begins to shake on Dino Island, Jen and Andy suspect the volcano is to blame. Eager to solve the mystery, our intrepid duo embark on an epic adventure to discover the source of the unusual rumbling sound and make a surprising discovery. Along the way, Andy meets not one, but two T rexes, a male and a female, while Jen finds a herd of Alamosaurus not far from the volcano.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Simon is taking Jess out for a birthday dinner, so Gramps is on babysitting duty. He's brought along Mr Willow's dogs, Trevor and Violet, for the evening. They look just like Waffle, and during a game of hide-and-sing the dogs all hide next door, causing confusion and chaos for poor Mrs Hobbs!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to blow a bubble just like her dads, but no matter how hard she tries, it won’t work. She makes a wish and creates a huge, magical bubble that floats around the park. As Rafi chases after it, the bubble spreads wonder wherever it goes. But when the bubble finally pops, Rafi is heartbroken. With help from her dads and friends, Rafi realises that bubbles aren’t meant to last forever, and that some of the most special moments are wonderful because they are fleeting.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When JoJo and Gran Gran visit the library, Terrence is about to launch a new Super Saleem book at a special story event later. Raya, Alfie and JoJo are going to dress up as superheroes. But while Raya and Alfie have already picked their superhero names and decided their superpowers, JoJo still needs to think about hers. Back at home, JoJo tries out her new superhero name before heading back to the library with Gran Gran.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Venus has attempted to redecorate the night sky, but now Sarah cannot find any of her favourite constellations.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small finds some 'space treasure' but doesn't know what it is for. Then Tiny too finds her own space treasure - a strange box. Only when they both realise that the two pieces might fit together do they get to see the unexpectedly beautiful results.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are singing a song. They hear the Tweeties singing and try to copy them. When the Tick Tock Clock chimes, they copy that noise too. As they make their way across Planet BeddyByes, they listen to the noises around them and collect sounds from their friends to create a wonderful friendship song.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Makka Pakka is in the garden looking for stones, but he can't find any. Igglepiggle is walking in the garden and comes across a stone, so he decides to find Makka Pakka and give the stone to him. Upsy Daisy finds a stone and gives it to Makka Pakka, then the Tombliboos find one, two, three stones and give them all to Makka Pakka. Makka Pakka's friends have given him five stones!

programme.desc: Sign along with your friend Mr Tumble as he tells a Bedtime Story all about friendship.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Central Italy meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck foraging truffles in Umbria before discovering how the Campanian Plain has been a hotbed of agricultural innovation for thousands of years, something he sees in today's precision herb farms. In a forest whose location is a closely-kept secret, he joins Alessandro and his dogs Moretta and Nena on the hunt for Black Gold! Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you - an indulgent, delicious truffle mac 'n' cheese. His journey then takes him to the ancient ruins of Paestum, a city born out of agricultural innovation, something the Campanian Plain is still at the cutting edge of today. He joins Guillermo to turn his hand to the carefully created lines of a precision farm that lead the way in the 21st century. After a hard day's work Tom cooks baked cod with parsley butter, gremolata and saffron rice to celebrate.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Central Italy meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck foraging truffles in Umbria before discovering how the Campanian Plain has been a hotbed of agricultural innovation for thousands of years, something he sees in today's precision herb farms. In a forest whose location is a closely-kept secret, he joins Alessandro and his dogs Moretta and Nena on the hunt for Black Gold! Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you - an indulgent, delicious truffle mac 'n' cheese. His journey then takes him to the ancient ruins of Paestum, a city born out of agricultural innovation, something the Campanian Plain is still at the cutting edge of today. He joins Guillermo to turn his hand to the carefully created lines of a precision farm that lead the way in the 21st century. After a hard day's work Tom cooks baked cod with parsley butter, gremolata and saffron rice to celebrate.

In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck foraging truffles in Umbria before discovering how the Campanian Plain has been a hotbed of agricultural innovation for thousands of years, something he sees in today's precision herb farms. In a forest whose location is a closely-kept secret, he joins Alessandro and his dogs Moretta and Nena on the hunt for Black Gold! Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you - an indulgent, delicious truffle mac 'n' cheese. His journey then takes him to the ancient ruins of Paestum, a city born out of agricultural innovation, something the Campanian Plain is still at the cutting edge of today. He joins Guillermo to turn his hand to the carefully created lines of a precision farm that lead the way in the 21st century. After a hard day's work Tom cooks baked cod with parsley butter, gremolata and saffron rice to celebrate.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Central Italy meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck foraging truffles in Umbria before discovering how the Campanian Plain has been a hotbed of agricultural innovation for thousands of years, something he sees in today's precision herb farms. In a forest whose location is a closely-kept secret, he joins Alessandro and his dogs Moretta and Nena on the hunt for Black Gold! Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you - an indulgent, delicious truffle mac 'n' cheese. His journey then takes him to the ancient ruins of Paestum, a city born out of agricultural innovation, something the Campanian Plain is still at the cutting edge of today. He joins Guillermo to turn his hand to the carefully created lines of a precision farm that lead the way in the 21st century. After a hard day's work Tom cooks baked cod with parsley butter, gremolata and saffron rice to celebrate.

The team discover a dispute at work over the death of a young lad when a safety rig failed - everyone believes that Owen was to blame despite an inquest failing to find fault. The victim's father admits that he wanted revenge but his alibi holds - Vera then spots an inconsistency in Ellie's statement that suggests that she was less sure of her husband's fidelity than she is admitting. programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Tom Kerridge is on the road in Central Italy meeting producers who are as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck he gets stuck foraging truffles in Umbria before discovering how the Campanian Plain has been a hotbed of agricultural innovation for thousands of years, something he sees in today's precision herb farms. In a forest whose location is a closely-kept secret, he joins Alessandro and his dogs Moretta and Nena on the hunt for Black Gold! Tom cooks up a feast to say thank you - an indulgent, delicious truffle mac 'n' cheese. His journey then takes him to the ancient ruins of Paestum, a city born out of agricultural innovation, something the Campanian Plain is still at the cutting edge of today. He joins Guillermo to turn his hand to the carefully created lines of a precision farm that lead the way in the 21st century. After a hard day's work Tom cooks baked cod with parsley butter, gremolata and saffron rice to celebrate.
